name: molvic
author: shops-money-swapping
description:
molvic v1 (direction: shops, money and swapping) - THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE TWO THINGS THAT ARE
ON EACH OTHER'S SHELF. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = THE SHELF UNIT DRAWN FROM THE FRONT, plus one caption line "<n> swap".
  5 shelves. Each shelf is a row "|X X   X Y X ...|" of 10-12 slots (one character per slot,
  separated by a space); under each shelf row is its edge "+-------+" as wide as the picture.
  A slot holds a good (a capital letter, one letter per kind of good) or is an empty gap " ".
  A SHELF BELONGS to the letter most of its goods are (margin >= 2 on every row of every clue,
  so the reading is never ambiguous); the five shelf letters are random and all different.
  A STRAY is a good standing on somebody else's shelf: 7-14 of them per clue, at most 4 on a
  shelf, and never two of the same kind on one shelf. Clue 226-266 chars, 11 lines + caption.

ANSWER = THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH THE SWAPPED GOODS PUT RIGHT. Each of the 2n swapped cells
becomes its own shelf's letter (the two goods have exchanged places, so each is now home).
Nothing else changes: same shelves, same edges, same gaps, same other strays. The answer is
UNIQUE per clue. The trailing "<n> swap" line may be kept or dropped; both score 1 (house rule
2026-09-05). Trailing spaces and trailing newlines are ignored.

RULE (one clause): TWO GOODS SWAP OVER IFF THEY STAND IN LINE - the same slot, one above the
other - AND EACH IS ON THE OTHER'S SHELF. Said in one breath: "those two are in line and each
one's on the other's shelf, so swap them." Formally, a stray of kind H[k] standing at (row i,
slot j) swaps iff the good at (row k, slot j) is of kind H[i]; the relation is symmetric, so
swaps come in pairs and n counts the pairs. Neither half alone is the rule: being in line with
another stray is not enough, and being on each other's shelf is not enough. The measurement -
"a vertical pair that is the wrong way round" - has no name, and it is NOT the shelf's famous
operation (which is "put everything back where it belongs"; that scores 0 here).

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. generate() plants, in every instance (audited over 3000-4000
clues):
  P1  TWO mutual pairs that are NOT in line (each on the other's shelf, different slots)
      -> kills the canonical blind guess "every mutual pair swaps"                       100 %
  P2  a pair of strays IN LINE that are NOT mutual (two legs of a three-way ring)
      -> kills "anything in line with another stray goes home"                           100 %
  P3  a three-way ring (A's good on B, B's on C, C's on A) -> kills "everything gets tidied"
      and "any ring resolves"                                                            100 %
  P4  swaps both next door (rows i, i+1) and right across the shop (rows i, i+2/3/4)
      -> kills "only touching shelves"                                            100 % (n>=2)
  P5  a shelf carrying both a mover and a stayer -> kills every shelf-level rule          100 %
  P6  a stray in line with a GAP on its own shelf -> kills "it goes back if there is a
      space for it in line"                                                              100 %
  P7  a stray in line with a plain, correctly-placed good on its own shelf                99 %
  P8  the movers are never simply the first 2n strays in reading order                   100 %
  P9  a third stray standing in one of the swapping columns -> kills "tidy that column"   99 %
The demo is a picture pair differing in exactly 2n characters, in n vertical pairs.

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 12.1 % of clues (measured over 3000 seeds) say "0 swap": nothing swaps
and the correct answer IS the clue returned unchanged, caption kept or dropped. Those clues look
exactly like the others (7-11 strays, mutual pairs, a ring - just none of them in line), so a
demo-less player who reads "a shelf unit, things in the wrong place, 2 swap" and echoes the
picture scores ~12 %, and so does every count-based guess. What the clue alone reveals about the
answer's SHAPE: it is this same shelf picture with a few letters put right, and the caption says
how many swaps - so a demo-less player always has a well-formed attempt to send.

WITNESS TABLE (2000 fresh clues, shipped scorer. Every template renders with the TRUE drawing
convention, i.e. it models a player who has seen a demo and holds the wrong rule):
  clue returned unchanged                                    11.8 %   <- the foothold
  clue unchanged, caption dropped                            11.8 %   <- same, lenient form
  n mutual pairs picked at random                            23.8 %   <- the top rival
  the leftmost columns holding two strays                    12.6 %
  2n strays at random                                        12.1 %
  the first 2n strays in reading order                       11.8 %
  the last 2n strays in reading order                        11.8 %
  the swapping columns tidied completely                     15.9 %
  mutual pairs on touching shelves only                       3.6 %
  in line with a stray on the shelf next door                 5.2 %
  tidy up: every stray put right                              0.0 %
  every shelf made uniform                                    0.0 %
  every mutual pair swaps (alignment ignored)                 0.0 %   <- the blind deduction
  every stray in line with a stray on its own shelf           0.0 %
  every ring resolves (2- and 3-way)                          0.0 %
  it goes home if there is a gap in line on its own shelf      0.0 %
  a plain good sits in line on its own shelf                   0.0 %
  the right swaps plus one mutual pair that is not in line      0.0 %
  the right swaps plus one lone stray put right                 0.0 %
  all the swaps but one cell left as it was                     0.0 %
  strays carried to a gap on their own shelf                    0.0 %
  the two letters written the wrong way round                 12.2 %  (= the 0-swap clues)
  the swapping strays rubbed out instead of swapped           12.2 %  (= the 0-swap clues)
  one fixed real answer for every clue                        0.1 %
  demo replay (another clue's answer)                         0.0 %
  TRUE RULE (solve)                                         100.0 %
No template exceeds 24 %. The one that pays is "mutuality found, alignment missed": with n
swapping pairs and 2 more mutual pairs that are not in line, guessing which n of the n+2 are
meant is 1/C(n+2,n), which with the 0-swap clues comes to ~24 % - a wrong-but-close rule scores
like a good foothold, and one demo (P1) shows the missing half.

WELL-FORMEDNESS (13 hand-built attacks x 800 clues, all 0.0 % unless noted): only one half of
each pair put right (12.2 %, = the 0-swap clues), all the swaps but one cell, the strays rubbed
out (12.2 %), strays carried to a gap, the whole shop tidied, every shelf made uniform, the two
letters written the wrong way round (12.2 %), the right swaps plus an extra one, a space pushed
into every shelf row, the answer sent twice, shelf edges removed, side walls removed, rows
reversed, gaps drawn as dots, lowercased, caption count changed, a junk line appended, a blank
line prepended, half the picture, the caption alone, the empty string, "1"*100, 4000 chars of
junk. Declared leniencies: trailing newlines, trailing whitespace on any row, caption present or
absent. The scorer rebuilds the whole expected picture from the clue and compares line by line,
so nothing about the rule can be smuggled through the form.

ENGINEERING (3000-4000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.15 ms, p99 0.36 ms, max 0.7 ms, 0 fallback
uses, 3000/3000 clues distinct and deterministic; solve mean 0.026 ms; score mean 0.03 ms on real
answers and 0.026 ms on junk (including 4000-char junk). Scorer 347/512 chars, solve 791/5000,
generate 5.3k/50000, clue 226-266 chars, solution 226-266 chars. n is 0 (12.1 %), 2 (42 %) or
3 (46 %). solve() output is forced (the answer is unique) but varies in every way that matters:
3000/3000 distinct, the shelf letters, widths, gaps and the swapped rows/slots are all random,
and the moved goods are never the first, last, tallest or leftmost strays.

INTENDED SPLIT. With a demo: the two pictures differ in 2n characters that fall into n vertical
pairs, so "same slot" is the first thing a player sees; the other half ("and each is on the
other's shelf") is forced by P2, and P1 stops the player who only sees mutuality. A player who
reads the picture as a shop ("those two are in each other's places") has it in one or two
rounds; a player who reads it as bookkeeping lands on "all the mutual pairs" and scores 24 %.
Without a demo: the clue is a drawn shelf unit with a verb and a count, so a well-formed attempt
is obvious (send the picture back with some strays put right) and the "0 swap" instances pay
~12 %; the natural blind deduction ("a swap needs two things to trade places, so it must be the
mutual pairs") scores 0 %, which is what puts this class on the edge of needing a demo.

LEVERS. Too easy: (a) require the caption dropped, which removes the identity foothold and the
offline checksum; (b) allow two strays of the same kind on one shelf, so "in line" has to be
disambiguated; (c) add a good whose kind is no shelf's kind (it belongs in another shop and
never moves). Too hard: (a) drop the alignment clause (swap every mutual pair - measured, that
is the blind-canonical guess and would make the class much easier); (b) draw one swap already
done in the clue as a worked instance; (c) drop to 3 shelves.
generate:
# THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE THINGS PUT BACK IN THE WRONG PLACE.
# Each shelf row holds goods (one capital letter per kind); a shelf belongs to the letter most
# of its goods are. A STRAY is a good standing on somebody else's shelf. Caption "<n> swap":
# n straight swaps happen. Two strays swap iff they stand IN LINE (the same slot) and each is
# on the other's shelf. Every clue plants the rest of that 2x2 and more:
#   TWO mutual pairs that are NOT in line, a pair in line that is NOT mutual (out of a
#   three-way ring), a stray in line with a gap, a stray in line with a plain good,
#   and swaps both next door and right across the shop.
AL = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWY"
FB = ("|K K   K K K M K K K|\n+-------------------+\n|M M M K M   M M M M|\n"
      "+-------------------+\n|T T T T P T   T T T|\n+-------------------+\n"
      "|P P   P P P T P P P|\n+-------------------+\n|S S S S S   S S S S|\n"
      "+-------------------+\n2 swap")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    zero = r.random() < 0.12                       # decided once, before any retry
    for _ in range(400):
        n = 0 if zero else r.randint(2, 3)         # swaps
        S = 5                                      # shelves
        W = r.randint(10, 12)                      # slots per shelf
        LT = r.sample(AL, S)                       # what each shelf is for
        up = [(a, b) for a in range(S) for b in range(a + 1, S)]
        r.shuffle(up)
        SWP, MM, rest = up[:n], up[n:n + 2], up[n + 2:]
        if n > 1 and not (any(b - a == 1 for a, b in SWP) and any(b - a > 1 for a, b in SWP)):
            continue                               # plant: one swap next door, one across the shop
        tri = [t for t in itertools.combinations(range(S), 3)
               if all(p in rest for p in ((t[0], t[1]), (t[1], t[2]), (t[0], t[2])))]
        if not tri:
            continue
        t = list(r.choice(tri))
        r.shuffle(t)
        pool = [p for p in rest if set(p) not in [{t[0], t[1]}, {t[1], t[2]}, {t[0], t[2]}]]
        r.shuffle(pool)
        G = [[LT[i]] * W for i in range(S)]
        occ = [set() for _ in range(S)]

        def put(host, home, j):                    # a good of LT[home] left on shelf `host`
            G[host][j] = LT[home]
            occ[host].add(j)

        def col(*rows):
            c = [j for j in range(W) if all(j not in occ[i] for i in rows)]
            return r.choice(c) if c else -1

        ok = True
        for a, b in SWP:                           # the swaps: in line and mutual
            j = col(a, b)
            if j < 0:
                ok = False
                break
            put(a, b, j)
            put(b, a, j)
        swc = [j for i in range(S) for j in occ[i]]
        for u, (a, b) in enumerate(MM):            # mutual, but NOT in line
            j1, j2 = col(a), col(b)
            if not u:                              # plant: a third stray standing in one of
                sa = [j for j in swc if j not in occ[a]]   # the swapping columns, so that
                sb = [j for j in swc if j not in occ[b]]   # "tidy that whole column" is
                if sa:                             # visibly wrong
                    j1 = r.choice(sa)
                elif sb:
                    j2 = r.choice(sb)
            if j1 < 0 or j2 < 0 or j1 == j2:
                ok = False
                break
            put(a, b, j1)
            put(b, a, j2)
        if not ok:
            continue
        j = col(t[0], t[1])                        # a three-way ring, two of it in line
        if j < 0:
            continue
        put(t[1], t[0], j)                         # in line with, but not mutual with,
        put(t[0], t[2], j)                         # the one below it
        j3 = col(t[2])
        if j3 < 0 or j3 == j:
            continue
        put(t[2], t[1], j3)
        for a, b in pool[:r.randint(0, 1)]:        # a lone stray or two for texture
            h, k = (a, b) if r.random() < .5 else (b, a)
            j = col(k)
            if j >= 0:
                put(k, h, j)
        if max(len(o) for o in occ) > 4:
            continue
        cand = [(k, j) for i in range(S) for j in occ[i]                # plant: a stray with a
                for k in [LT.index(G[i][j])] if G[k][j] == LT[k]]       # gap in line on its own
        if not cand:                                                    # shelf (nothing there
            continue                                                    # to swap with)
        k, j = r.choice(cand)
        G[k][j] = " "
        occ[k].add(j)
        for i in range(S):                         # more gaps: never on a stray
            fr = [j for j in range(W) if j not in occ[i]]
            for j in r.sample(fr, min(len(fr), r.randint(1, 2))):
                G[i][j] = " "
        sw = set()
        for i in range(S):
            for j in range(W):
                x = G[i][j]
                if x not in " " + LT[i] and G[LT.index(x)][j] == LT[i]:
                    sw.add((i, j))
        if len(sw) != 2 * n:                       # exactly the intended swaps, nothing else
            continue
        bar = "+" + "-" * (2 * W - 1) + "+"
        out = []
        for i in range(S):
            out.append("|" + " ".join(G[i]) + "|")
            out.append(bar)
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n" + str(n) + " swap"
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    P = clue.split("\n")
    T = P.pop()                                   # the "<n> swap" caption, copied through
    R = P[::2]                                    # the shelf rows (odd lines are shelf edges)
    H = [max(set(x) - set(" |"), key=x.count) for x in R]     # what each shelf is for
    E = []
    for i, x in enumerate(R):
        g = list(x)
        for j, y in enumerate(x):
            if y not in " |" + H[i]:              # a good on somebody else's shelf
                if R[H.index(y)][j] == H[i]:      # in line with one on its shelf, the other way round
                    g[j] = H[i]                   # the two of them swap over
        E.append("".join(g))
    return "\n".join([P[i] if i % 2 else E[i // 2] for i in range(len(P))]) + "\n" + T
